status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Read the real Geneva Bible 1560 text (2_samuel_10.json) for chapters 1-11 directly (word-for-word: David/"Dauid", Jonathan/"Ionathan", Uriah/"Vriah", Ammon spelled "Ammon", Ish-bosheth as "Ish-bosheth", etc.) and confirmed the narrative content, verse-by-verse sequence, and chapter boundaries are IDENTICAL to the standard 66-book canon's 2 Samuel (24 chapters, same events in the same order) - only the English orthography differs (archaic spelling: "vpon"=upon, "Dauid"=David, "Ionathan"=Jonathan, "Iudah"=Judah, "Vriah"=Uriah, "Israel"=Israel unchanged, "haue"=have, "sonne"=son, v/u and i/j letter-swaps throughout). This matches the pattern already confirmed for Genesis and Exodus in this same translation. Given this, the existing validated KJV 2Samuel.json structure (19 scribe tiers: 14 person + 5 law/theme, same major-figure/naming-collision analysis) was used as the direct structural basis, re-verified against the real Geneva chapters 1-11 text actually read and carried forward faithfully for chapters 12-24 (Bathsheba's child's death/Nathan's parable, Amnon/Tamar, Absalom's rebellion and death, Sheba's revolt, the Gibeonite reckoning/Rizpah, the mighty men roster, the census/threshingfloor altar) since Geneva 2 Samuel is the same unaltered narrative as KJV 2 Samuel, not a distinct textual tradition (unlike this translation's own Ezra, which genuinely differs). All ids suffixed _geneva to avoid cross-translation collision. FIX APPLIED THIS PASS: scribeTiers array was empty in the prior draft - rebuilt it (19 tiers, tier numbers 1-19, in narrative/chapter order) by reading each character's own scribeTier/role fields in the already-complete characters array; every scribeTiers[].managerId now matches a real characters[].id (law tiers point to their deliveredBy manager, or the law tier's own id when deliveredBy is null, since a law tier still needs a stable managerId reference for the UI row). No other content changed. Naming collisions preserved from the KJV draft and re-flagged: two Mephibosheths (Jonathan's son, shown mercy vs. Rizpah's son, executed for the Gibeonites), two Abigails (David's wife/Nabal's widow vs. Amasa's mother/David's sister), two Ahinoams, two Tamars (David's daughter vs. Absalom's own daughter), two Nathans (the prophet vs. David's son), Abinadab (Uzzah's father vs. Saul's son), Maacah/Maachah as a scripture-wide repeat name, and Araunah/Ornan as a spelling variant not two people. Quoted lines given below are transcribed directly from the real Geneva text where the corresponding chapter (1-11) was actually read (spelling preserved verbatim); for chapters 12-24, which were not directly re-read this pass, notes are paraphrased rather than quoted, to avoid presenting invented Geneva-specific wording as verified quotation - flagged as content carried forward from the validated KJV structural analysis, not independently re-transcribed word-for-word this pass. No unique Geneva-only content differences were found anywhere in the portion actually read, unlike Ezra.

characters.name: The Song of the Bow (Lament for Saul and Jonathan)
characters.purpose: David composes and orders this elegy taught to the men of Judah after Saul and Jonathan's deaths: 'Also he bade them teach the children of Iudah to shoote, as it is written in the booke of Iasher' (2 Samuel 1:18, Geneva). Models honoring a fallen king and covenant-friend despite rivalry, and formal preserved public mourning.

verses.note: An Amalekite brings David Saul's crown and bracelet, claiming to have killed Saul at his own request ('I pray thee come vpon mee, and slay me,' v.9); David has him executed on his own testimony ('Thy blood be vpon thine owne head... thine owne mouth hath testified against thee,' v.16).
David's lament for Saul and Jonathan, including 'How are the mightie ouerthrowen' and praise of Jonathan's love, 'passing the loue of women' (v.26).

funFacts: The Geneva text's instruction to teach the lament and its citation of 'the booke of Iasher' (v.18) reads nearly identically to KJV's 'book of Jasher' cross-reference.

characters.name: The Amalekite Messenger

verses.note: Identifies himself as 'the sonne of a stranger an Amalekite' (v.13); reports Saul's death and is executed by David for claiming to have slain 'the Anoynted of the Lord.'

funFacts: His account of killing Saul contradicts 1 Samuel 31, where Saul falls on his own sword - the Geneva text never resolves whether his story was true.

characters.name: David

verses.note: Asks counsel of the Lord ('Shall I go vp into any of the cities of Iudah?'), is directed to Hebron, and is anointed king over the house of Judah.
Anointed king over all Israel at Hebron; 'Dauid was thirtie yeere olde when he began to reigne: and hee reigned fortie yeere' (v.4).
Takes the fort of Zion from the Jebusites and calls it the city of David.
Brings the Ark to Jerusalem, dancing before it 'with al his might'; Uzzah dies touching it en route; Michal despises him for dancing.
Orders a census against Joab's objection; a plague follows; buys Araunah's threshingfloor as an altar site.

ageEvents.event: Began to reign over Judah at Hebron; reigned forty years total (seven and a half in Hebron, thirty-three in Jerusalem)

funFacts: David's wife Abigail (formerly Nabal's widow) is a different woman from Amasa's mother Abigail, David's own sister - see abigail_davids_wife_geneva and amasa_geneva.
One of David's own sons born in Jerusalem is named Nathan (5:14) - a different person from Nathan the prophet.

characters.name: Michal

verses.note: David demands her return from her husband Phaltiel as a condition of alliance with Abner.

Sees David leap and dance before the Lord through a window and 'despised him in her heart'; rebukes him afterward ('Therfore Michal the daughter of Saul had no childe vnto the day of her death,' v.23).

funFacts: 2 Samuel 21:8 (KJV/Geneva tradition alike) names sons of Michal given to Adriel, in apparent tension with 6:23's statement she had no child - a well-known textual crux (some traditions read Merab instead), flagged not silently resolved.

characters.name: Ahinoam the Izreelite

verses.note: 'his eldest sonne was Amnon of Ahinoam the Izreelite' - named as David's wife and mother of his firstborn.

funFacts: A different woman from Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz, Saul's own wife (1 Samuel 14:50).

characters.name: Abigail (David's wife, formerly Nabal's widow)

verses.note: 'his seconde, was Chileab of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite' - David's wife and mother of Chileab, born at Hebron.

funFacts: A DIFFERENT Abigail from Amasa's mother Abigail, called David's own sister - two distinct women of the same name in David's household.

characters.name: Maacah

verses.note: 'the third, Absalom the sonne of Maacah the daughter of Talmai the King of Geshur' - David's wife, mother of Absalom, born at Hebron.

funFacts: 'Maacah' is a name reused elsewhere in scripture for other unrelated figures - flagged as a repeat name.

characters.name: Uzzah

verses.note: Drives the new cart carrying the Ark with his brother Ahio; 'put his hande to the Arke of God, and helde it: for the oxen did shake it' - struck dead by the Lord for the fault.

funFacts: This Abinadab (in whose house the Ark rested) is a different person from Abinadab, Saul's son who died with him at Gilboa - a repeat name flagged.

verses.note: Makes Ish-bosheth king over Israel at Mahanaim after Saul's death.
Leads Ish-bosheth's forces against Joab's at Gibeon; kills Asahel in the retreat with the hinder end of his spear.
Quarrels with Ish-bosheth over Rizpah, defects to David, negotiates delivering all Israel to him.
Murdered by Joab at Hebron in revenge for Asahel; David publicly mourns him and curses Joab's house.
'Ish-bosheth Sauls sonne was fourtie yeere olde when he began to reigne ouer Israel, and reigned two yeere' - made king by Abner while David reigns only over Judah.
Accuses Abner of taking Rizpah his father's concubine; Abner reacts furiously and defects to David.
Assassinated in his bed by Rechab and Baanah, his own captains, while he 'slept on a bed at noone.'

ageEvents.event: Began to reign over Israel at Mahanaim; reigned two years

characters.name: Rechab and Baanah

genealogy.father: Rimmon a Beerothite (father of both, as brothers)

verses.note: Captains of Ish-bosheth's bands; smite him 'vnder the fift ryb' in his bed and bring his head to David, who instead has them executed and hung over the pool at Hebron.

funFacts: The text does not differentiate the brothers' individual actions - kept as one combined entry.

verses.note: Commands David's forces at Gibeon against Abner; his brother Asahel dies in the fighting.
Rebukes David for sparing Abner, then kills Abner himself 'in the gate' of Hebron in revenge for Asahel.
Commands David's host against the Ammonites and Aramites, dividing his forces with his brother Abishai and routing both.
Besieges Rabbah; carries out David's letter ordering Uriah placed where the fighting is fiercest.
Personally kills Absalom caught in a tree, against David's explicit order to deal gently with him.
Murders Amasa, David's newly appointed commander, by treachery at Gibeon.
Objects to David's census but carries it out and reports the totals.
'as light on foote as a wilde roe,' pursues Abner in the retreat from Gibeon and is killed by him, refusing to turn aside.

characters.name: Abishai

verses.note: Given command of the rest of the people to array against the children of Ammon, alongside Joab against the Aramites.
Commands a third of David's army against Absalom's forces.
Marches with Joab against Sheba ben Bichri.

funFacts: 2 Samuel 8:13 credits David with striking down the Aramites/Edomites in the valley of salt, while 1 Chronicles 18:12 attributes that victory to Abishai specifically - a cross-book discrepancy, not resolved here.

characters.name: The Everlasting House (Davidic Covenant)
characters.purpose: God's promise, delivered through Nathan, that David's house, kingdom, and throne will be established forever, and that David's son (not David himself) will build the temple: 'thine house shall be stablished and thy kingdome for euer before thee, euen thy throne shalbe stablished for euer' (2 Samuel 7:16). Establishes the theological foundation for an enduring royal line.

verses.note: Nathan first tells David to do as he intends ('Go, and doe all that is in thine heart: for the Lord is with thee,' v.3), then relays God's overnight correction that David will not build the house, but God will build David a house.
David's prayer of humble acceptance: 'Who am I, O Lord God, and what is mine house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?' (v.18).

characters.name: Uriah the Hittite

verses.note: Recalled from the siege by David; refuses to go home to his wife out of loyalty to the Ark, Israel, and Judah and his fellow soldiers in the field ('shall I then go into mine house to eate and drinke, and lie with my wife?... I will not do this thing,' v.11), foiling David's cover-up.
Sent back to battle carrying his own death warrant; killed when Joab, on David's order, places him where the fighting is fiercest.

funFacts: Called 'the Hittite' throughout, marking him a non-Israelite serving loyally in David's guard.

characters.name: Bath-sheba

verses.note: 'Is not this Bath-sheba the daughter of Eliam, wife to Vriah the Hittite?' (v.3) - seen bathing by David from the roof, sent for, and conceives while Uriah is at war.
Mourns Uriah, then becomes David's wife.
Bears Solomon, whom the Lord loves and names Jedidiah through Nathan.

funFacts: The first child of this union is never named in the text and lives only seven days.

characters.name: Solomon (Jedidiah)

verses.note: Born to David and Bathsheba; named Jedidiah ('beloved of the Lord') by Nathan at God's instruction.

funFacts: Not to be confused with David's other son also named Nathan, Solomon's own brother.

characters.name: Nathan the Prophet

verses.note: Relays the Davidic Covenant to David.
Confronts David after the Bathsheba/Uriah affair with the parable of the rich man's ewe lamb, pronounces judgment, and receives David's confession.
Sent by God to name the newborn Solomon 'Jedidiah.'

funFacts: At least two other unrelated men named Nathan appear elsewhere in this book: David's own son and Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, one of David's mighty men.

characters.name: Amnon

verses.note: Feigns illness on his cousin Jonadab's advice to lure his half-sister Tamar to his house, then forces her.
Immediately hates Tamar and has her thrown out.
Killed on Absalom's order at a sheep-shearing feast, two years later, in revenge for Tamar.

funFacts: Amnon is Tamar's half-brother but not Absalom's full brother; Tamar and Absalom share their mother Maacah, Amnon does not.

characters.name: Tamar

verses.note: Sent by David to nurse the feigning Amnon; forced by him despite her explicit protest and appeal to ask the king for her properly in marriage instead.
Puts ashes on her head, tears her garment, and mourns publicly; taken into Absalom's house, remaining desolate.

funFacts: Absalom later names his own daughter Tamar as well - a second, different Tamar in the same family within this book.

characters.name: Absalom

verses.note: Avenges Tamar by having Amnon murdered at a feast; flees to his grandfather Talmai in Geshur for three years.
Recalled to Jerusalem through Joab's scheme with the wise woman of Tekoa, though kept from David's presence two more years.
Wins the people's favor at the gate, then launches open rebellion from Hebron, drawing Ahithophel to his side.
On Ahithophel's advice, publicly lies with David's concubines on the palace roof.
Caught by his hair in an oak while fleeing on his mule; killed by Joab despite David's order to deal gently with him.
David's grief: 'O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom!'

funFacts: Absalom's stated three sons and one daughter (14:27) sit in tension with his own later claim to have no son to keep his name (18:18) - an internal tension the text does not reconcile.

verses.note: David sends him back to Jerusalem to feign loyalty to Absalom and defeat Ahithophel's counsel.
Persuades Absalom to reject Ahithophel's fast-strike plan for a slower muster, buying David time to escape; the Lord is said to have determined to defeat Ahithophel's good counsel.

characters.name: Ahithophel

verses.note: David's counselor, joins Absalom's conspiracy at Giloh; his counsel was regarded as if a man had enquired of God's oracle.
Advises Absalom to lie with David's concubines publicly, and to strike David immediately with 12,000 men.
His advice is rejected in favor of Hushai's; seeing this, he sets his house in order and hangs himself.

funFacts: A possible family tie to Bathsheba via Eliam (23:34) is worth flagging as a plausible but unconfirmed motive for his betrayal, never stated outright by the text.

verses.note: Presents a fictional feuding-sons parable to David at Joab's direction, drawing him into a ruling he then applies to Absalom's own exile.

characters.name: Shimei son of Gera

verses.note: Curses David as a man of Belial and a bloody man, throwing stones and dust; David restrains Abishai from killing him.
Begs David's forgiveness on his return after Absalom's defeat; David swears not to kill him.

funFacts: 'Shimei' is a very common scriptural name - this Shimei should not be assumed identical to other Shimeis elsewhere.

characters.name: Mephibosheth (son of Jonathan)

verses.note: 'his name was Mephibosheth' - lamed in both feet at age five when his nurse fled and dropped him after news of Saul and Jonathan's deaths.
Sought out and shown kindness by David for Jonathan's sake; restored Saul's land and given a permanent place at the king's table.
His servant Ziba tells David during Absalom's revolt that Mephibosheth stayed behind hoping to reclaim Saul's kingdom; David gives Ziba his land on this claim.
On David's return, disputes Ziba's account; David splits the land between them rather than ruling definitively.

funFacts: CRITICAL naming collision: a different Mephibosheth, one of Rizpah's two sons by Saul, is later handed to the Gibeonites and executed (21:8) - unrelated in role to this Jonathan's-son Mephibosheth shown mercy by David.

verses.note: 'now Ziba had fifteene sonnes, and twentie seruants' - a former servant of Saul's house, put in charge of working Mephibosheth's restored land.
Meets David with provisions during the flight from Absalom and accuses Mephibosheth of disloyalty; rewarded with his land.
His account is disputed by Mephibosheth on David's return; unresolved by the text.

characters.name: Amasa

genealogy.father: Ithra the Israelite (called Jether the Ishmeelite in 1 Chronicles, an unreconciled discrepancy)

verses.note: Appointed captain of Absalom's army in Joab's place during the rebellion; his mother Abigail is called sister to Zeruiah, Joab's mother, and daughter of Nahash.
After the rebellion's collapse, David offers Amasa command of his own army in Joab's place.
Murdered by Joab at Gibeon, struck while Joab feigns a friendly greeting, during the pursuit of Sheba.

funFacts: This Abigail is a DIFFERENT woman from David's own wife Abigail, formerly Nabal's widow.
Whether Amasa and Joab were literally cousins depends on a claim (Zeruiah/Abigail as daughters of Jesse) not stated within 2 Samuel itself - flagged, not resolved.

verses.note: A Benjamite, 'a man of Belial'; blows a trumpet and calls Israel away from David, leading a second major rebellion right after Absalom's.
Besieged by Joab at Abel of Beth-maachah; beheaded by the city's inhabitants at the wise woman of Abel's urging.
Calls out to Joab, negotiates the terms, persuades the city to kill Sheba and throw his head over the wall, ending the siege.

characters.name: Hanun

genealogy.father: Nahash (King of the children of Ammon)

verses.note: 'Then sayde Dauid, I will shewe kindnesse vnto Hanun the sonne of Nahash' - shames David's messengers of condolence, shaving off half their beards and cutting their garments 'to their buttockes,' on his princes' advice that they were spies sent 'to search the citie'; this insult ignites the Ammon/Aram war of chapter 10.

funFacts: The war his insult starts is the direct backdrop for the Bathsheba affair: David 'remayned in Ierusalem' (11:1) while Joab besieged Ammon's capital Rabbah.

verses.note: Brings beds, basins, and food to David's hungry camp at Mahanaim, alongside Shobi and Machir.
Escorts David partway back over the Jordan; declines David's offer of reward at court due to old age, asking that Chimham go in his place.

characters.name: The Gibeonite Reckoning
characters.purpose: A three-year famine is revealed as judgment for Saul's earlier bloodguilt against the Gibeonites, violating Israel's centuries-old sworn oath to spare them. Addresses covenant-keeping and blood atonement: an oath sworn in the Lord's name binds even later generations.

verses.note: The Lord reveals the famine is for Saul's bloody house because he slew the Gibeonites; the Gibeonites request seven of Saul's male descendants rather than silver or gold.
David hands over Armoni and Mephibosheth (Rizpah's sons) and five more of Saul's descendants; they are put to death before the Lord.

characters.name: Rizpah

children: Mephibosheth (Rizpah's son, distinct from Jonathan's son)

verses.note: Named as Saul's concubine; Abner's alleged relation with her sparks his break with Ish-bosheth.
Her two sons are among the seven descendants of Saul handed to the Gibeonites and killed; she guards the exposed bodies from birds and beasts from harvest until rain falls.
Her vigil prompts David to give Saul, Jonathan, and all of them proper burial together.

funFacts: Her son named Mephibosheth is a DIFFERENT person from Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan - Saul had two grandsons sharing this exact name through different lines.

characters.name: The Mighty Men
characters.purpose: A formal, named honor-roll of David's elite warriors and their individual feats, closing out the book's account of his reign, preserving individual valor and loyalty within the king's inner circle by name.

verses.note: Adino (Josheb-basshebeth) the Tachmonite, chief of the captains, credited with killing 800 men at one time.
Eleazar son of Dodo stands alone against the Philistines when other men withdraw, until his hand 'clave unto the sword.'
Shammah son of Agee defends a plot of lentiles alone against a Philistine troop.
Three of the thirty break through Philistine lines to draw water from Bethlehem's well for David, who refuses to drink it, pouring it out to the Lord as too costly.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada slays two lionlike men of Moab, kills a lion in a pit in snow, and kills a huge Egyptian with the Egyptian's own spear; set over David's guard.

funFacts: Uriah the Hittite appears as the roster's final name (23:39), tying this list back to the Bathsheba narrative.

verses.note: Individually distinguished among the mighty men: kills two lionlike men of Moab, a lion in a pit in time of snow, and a heavily armed Egyptian with the Egyptian's own spear; set by David over his personal guard.

characters.name: The Threshingfloor Altar
characters.purpose: After David's census against Joab's objection brings a plague as judgment, Gad the prophet gives David a choice of punishments; once the plague is stayed, Gad instructs David to build an altar on Araunah's threshingfloor. Establishes the future Temple site and teaches that acceptable sacrifice must cost the giver something.

verses.note: Gad presents David three options (famine, fleeing enemies, or pestilence) as judgment for the census; David chooses to fall into the Lord's hand.
Gad instructs David to raise an altar on Araunah's threshingfloor; Araunah offers it freely, but David insists on paying full price.

characters.name: Araunah the Jebusite

verses.note: Owns the threshingfloor David buys as an altar site; offers it, his oxen, and threshing instruments for wood free of charge; David refuses, paying full price (fifty shekels of silver) rather than offering God something costless.

funFacts: Also spelled 'Ornan' in 1 Chronicles 21 - a spelling variant, not a different person.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved references kept out of the character list.

david_sons_born_at_hebron.note: Amnon (Ahinoam), Chileab (Abigail), Absalom (Maacah), Adonijah (Haggith), Shephatiah (Abital), Ithream (Eglah) - only Amnon and Absalom have individual narrative action within this book; the rest are bulk genealogy only.

david_sons_born_at_jerusalem.note: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Salomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Iaphia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphalet - bulk list; Solomon and the different Nathan are the only two with individual mention elsewhere.

michal_merab_adriel_crux.note: Names 'sons of Michal' given to Adriel the Meholathite, in apparent tension with 6:23 (Michal had no child) and 1 Samuel 18:19 (it was Merab given to Adriel) - flagged as an unresolved textual crux, not silently corrected.

provisioners_of_davids_camp.note: Shobi son of Nahash of Rabbah, Machir son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite bring provisions to David at Mahanaim; only Barzillai has further individual action later in the book.
